newsitem.title: INDIA: India's external trade to pick up by year-end.
newsitem.headline: India's external trade to pick up by year-end.

text.p: Growth in India's external trade, which slowed down in the first half of 1996/97, will pick up gradually in the second half, Crosby Securities said on Wednesday.
"An industrial revival will suck in more imports even as exports begin to rise," it said in its September South Asia Economic Review.
Crosby said it expected a strong performance in agricultural exports, which grew 67 percent year on year in April-July 1996/97.
"This will continue the rest of the year because of a good monsoon which will ensure growth of the farm sector and thereby increase the exportable sector," it said.

"Overall, we expect exports and imports to expand 16 percent in FY97, compared to our earlier 19 percent forecast. This will result in current account deficit worth $6.0 billion (1.8 percent of GDP) which we consider sustainable," it said.
